- [ ] **[UDT-022]** `[Resource Leak]` CancellationTokenSource not disposed in DriverKeyListener.cs:55. *Root Cause*: StopAsync() sets _cancellationTokenSource = null after CancelAsync() but never calls .Dispose(). The CTS's internal timer/registration resources leak until GC finalizer runs. Unlike ThrottleLastDispatcher (which defers to Dispose()), DriverKeyListener implements IListener not IDisposable — no Dispose() path exists. *Suggested Fix*: Add using or explicit dispose: ar cts = _cancellationTokenSource; _cancellationTokenSource = null; cts?.Dispose(); (dispose after null to avoid race with StartAsync)._Audit log (pass-17776, 2026-07-08, Codex): Reporter-only. - [ ] **[UDT-023]** `[Threading / Unhandled Exception]` PluginHotReload.cs:434 — async void FileSystemWatcher.Changed handler wraps OnPluginFileChanged without try-catch. *Root Cause*: The lambda `async (sender, e) => { ... await OnPluginFileChanged(pluginId, e.FullPath); }` is implicitly async void (event handler delegate). If ReloadPluginAsync (called inside) throws, the exception escapes to the SynchronizationContext or AppDomain.UnhandledException — crashing the process. This violates Pillar A (no unhandled exceptions from async void). *Suggested Fix*: Wrap the entire lambda body in try-catch that logs via PluginLog.Trace:
```
watcher.Changed += async (sender, e) =>
{
    try
    {
        if (e.ChangeType == WatcherChangeTypes.Changed)
            await OnPluginFileChanged(pluginId, e.FullPath);
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        if (Log.Instance.IsTraceEnabled)
            Log.Instance.Trace($"Error handling file change for plugin {pluginId}", ex);
    }
};
```_Audit log (pass-19880, 2026-07-08, Codex): Reporter-only. UDT: CA=24; hex=0; catch=0. PLG: hex=0; catch=2. VSR: unwrap=0; static=0; OS=0; Virt=9. No new defects. Queues=0. Next: UDT-011, PLG-006, VSR-012._

- [ ] **[UDT-024]** `[Threading / Lock Misuse]` AutomationProcessor.cs:185,586 — `lock (_ioLock)` used on `AsyncLock` (NeoSmart.AsyncLock). *Root Cause*: `_ioLock` is typed `AsyncLock` (line 31) which is designed for `await _ioLock.LockAsync()`. The C# `lock()` statement uses `Monitor.Enter`/`Exit` on the object itself — this does NOT synchronize with `AsyncLock`'s internal semaphore. Result: Dispose (line 586) can acquire `lock(_ioLock)` and null-out `_cts` concurrently while `RunAsync` (line 185) holds the AsyncLock and reads `_cts`, causing a NullReferenceException or CTS use-after-dispose. *Suggested Fix*: Replace `lock(_ioLock)` with `await _ioLock.LockAsync()` at call sites, or if sync access is needed, use a separate `object _ctsLock = new()` for the CTS swap:
```
// In RunAsync (line 185):
lock (_ctsLock)
{
    oldCts = _cts;
    _cts = new CancellationTokenSource();
}
// In Dispose (line 586):
lock (_ctsLock)
{
    ctsToDispose = _cts;
    _cts = null;
}
